concepts.def: Number of confederates in a study trial.
Whether all confederates agree on a wrong answer.
Confederate who gives the correct answer.

Conforming to fit in, as in Asch's setup.
Conforming when unsure of the right answer.

walkthroughs.body_html: Asch varied the number of confederates. Conformity rose sharply from 1 to 3 confederates (around 30%), then plateaued. Beyond 3-4 confederates, adding more had little extra effect on conformity rates.

When one confederate gave the correct answer (a dissenter), conformity fell from 37% to about 5%. Breaking unanimity releases the participant from pressure — even an incorrect dissenter reduces conformity.
When lines were closer in length and harder to judge, conformity rose. Participants became unsure and relied on others — this is ISI. So Asch's setup can show NSI or ISI depending on conditions.
